note: Shipped harmonization settings (read by calibrate.py, flags.py, validate.py). Chosen 15 Nov 2026 by the search in docs/experiments_2012.md (incl. a 166,404-combination full grid): each setting kept only if it passed more checks with no regressions, the held-back areas no worse, and held-out errors no worse.

why.static_mask: F6: FIRMS types the same volcano or flare differently per sensor (Holuhraun 2014: VIIRS 'vegetation', MODIS 'static'). A 0.05 deg place either sensor family types static (>= 50% of its detections) is static for every sensor and year, plus a one-cell margin around places VIIRS types static (MODIS's coarse pixels scatter detections of the same source). A margin around MODIS-only places too scored about the same (3.93% vs 3.95% held-out) but moved 7.1% instead of 2.8% of Mato Grosso's fires into 'industrial'.
why.n0_factor.k_s: F8: S-NPP and NOAA-20 carry the same instrument, so the S-NPP -> NOAA-20 factor is pooled almost to its month x day/night value; its own held-out error drops from 2.05% to 1.80% (region x month).
why.month_pool (not used): F10 pooling of neighbouring months lowered the world held-out error a little (4.03% -> 3.95% at 0.10) but in held-out years it biased the start-of-season months where a quiet month sits next to a busy one: Punjab April predicted/actual 1.25 -> 1.71, September 0.99 -> 0.61; Haryana September 1.08 -> 0.73. Season start and critical months are what the app shows, so it is off. Blending ratios instead of counts was worse (4.27%, Haryana fails).
why.static_cfg: Industrial / persistent sites get their own fit: MODIS sees few of the small flares and plants VIIRS sees (California: ~6,000 VIIRS vs ~40 MODIS detections a year), so (F1) each 5 deg block x month x day/night keeps its VIIRS industrial total, (F4) fitted on 2012-15, the years nearest the MODIS-only record, (F12) day and night share a ratio because a flare burns around the clock, (F8) n0 300 because cell-level industrial counts are noise. Industrial held-out error (region x month) 23.4% -> 20.4%, bias -17% -> +1%. Chosen from 288 industrial settings on top of the shipped vegetation fit: passes California (+17% -> +1%) with no regression and the 6 held-back areas unchanged (5/6 within 5%).
